items.question: Why is 我今天比較是忙 not right?
items.answer: 比較 goes before the quality 忙, and 是 is not needed: 我今天比較忙.

items.question: Can I put 很 and 比較 together?
items.answer: No. Choose one degree word: 今天的天氣比較熱. 很 would say “very hot”, not “hotter than the other day”.

items.question: Where does 比較 go when the sentence uses 得?
items.answer: After 跑得: 哥哥跑得比較快. 比較 comes before the quality 快, not before 跑.

text.traditional: A：誰比較瘦？B：姊姊比較瘦，妹妹比較胖。

text.pinyin: A: Shéi bǐjiào shòu? B: Jiějie bǐjiào shòu, mèimei bǐjiào pàng.

text.traditional: A：坐飛機比較舒服，還是坐車比較舒服？B：我覺得坐飛機比較舒服。

text.english: A: Is flying more comfortable, or is taking a car more comfortable? B: I think flying is more comfortable.

text.english: A: Between you two, who sings better? B: I think he sings better.

items.question: Where does 能 go — before the subject or before the verb?
items.answer: Before the verb: 他能來嗎？ 能 does not come before the subject.

items.question: Where does 只 go in 只能?
items.answer: 只 comes before 能: 他只能走. Do not put 只 after the verb.

items.question: The picture shows an injured man. Do I say 他能跑 or 他不能跑?
items.answer: Use 不能: 他受傷了，他不能跑. The injury blocks the action.

right.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, tā bù néng pǎo.
right.english: He is injured; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 鳥能飛，人不能飛。
text.simplified: 鸟能飞，人不能飞。
text.pinyin: Niǎo néng fēi, rén bù néng fēi.
text.english: Birds can fly; humans cannot fly.

text.traditional: 他現在只能走，不能跑。
text.simplified: 他现在只能走，不能跑。
text.pinyin: Tā xiànzài zhǐ néng zǒu, bù néng pǎo.
text.english: He can only walk right now; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因為不能睡覺。
text.simplified: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因为不能睡觉。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù néng hē tài duō kāfēi, yīnwèi bù néng shuìjiào.
text.english: I cannot drink too much coffee, because I won’t be able to sleep.

text.traditional: 現在是上課時間，老師說我們不能看手機。
text.simplified: 现在是上课时间，老师说我们不能看手机。

text.english: It is class time now; the teacher said we cannot look at our phones.

text.traditional: A：在捷運上能吃東西嗎？B：不可以吃東西。
text.simplified: A：在捷运上能吃东西吗？B：不可以吃东西。
text.pinyin: A: Zài jiéyùn shàng néng chī dōngxi ma? B: Bù kěyǐ chī dōngxi.
text.english: A: Can you eat food on the MRT? B: You cannot eat food.

text.traditional: A：我能在這裡用電腦嗎？B：可以，沒問題。
text.simplified: A：我能在这里用电脑吗？B：可以，没问题。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ néng zài zhèlǐ yòng diànnǎo ma? B: Kěyǐ, méi wèntí.
text.english: A: Can I use a computer here? B: Yes, no problem.

text.traditional: 今天我有中文課，不能跟你們去玩。
text.simplified: 今天我有中文课，不能跟你们去玩。

text.english: I have Chinese class today, so I cannot go out with you all.

text.traditional: A：那個地方很遠，我們十點鐘能到嗎？B：沒問題，坐捷運很快。
text.simplified: A：那个地方很远，我们十点钟能到吗？B：没问题，坐捷运很快。
text.pinyin: A: Nàge dìfāng hěn yuǎn, wǒmen shí diǎn zhōng néng dào ma? B: Méi wèntí, zuò jiéyùn hěn kuài.
text.english: A: That place is very far; can we arrive by ten o’clock? B: No problem; taking the MRT is very fast.

text.traditional: A：明天他能來嗎？B：他不能來，因為他女朋友的媽媽要請他吃飯。
text.simplified: A：明天他能来吗？B：他不能来，因为他女朋友的妈妈要请他吃饭。
text.pinyin: A: Míngtiān tā néng lái ma? B: Tā bù néng lái, yīnwèi tā nǚpéngyǒu de māma yào qǐng tā chīfàn.
text.english: A: Can he come tomorrow? B: He cannot come, because his girlfriend’s mother invited him to dinner.

items.question: Where does 先 go — before the first action or after it?
items.answer: Before it. 先 + first action, 再 + next action: 我先看書，再做功課.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān kànshū, zài zuò gōngkè.
right.english: I read first, then do homework.

items.question: Is the second marker 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then” in a sequence. 在 is the “at / happening now” word: 我先回家，再去圖書館.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān huí jiā, zài qù túshūguǎn.
right.english: I go home first, then go to the library.

items.question: Where does 再 go when the second person is named?
items.answer: After the second subject: 姐姐先唱，妹妹再唱. Do not put 再 before 妹妹.

right.pinyin: Jiějie xiān chàng, mèimei zài chàng.
right.english: Older sister sings first, then younger sister sings.

text.english: A: Between you two, who speaks first? B: He speaks first, then I speak.

text.traditional: A：我要怎麼到那家飯店？B：你要先坐捷運，再坐公車。
text.simplified: A：我要怎么到那家饭店？B：你要先坐捷运，再坐公车。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ yào zěnme dào nà jiā fàndiàn? B: Nǐ yào xiān zuò jiéyùn, zài zuò gōngchē.
text.english: A: How do I get to that hotel? B: First take the MRT, then take a bus.

text.traditional: A：你明天想要做什麼？B：我想先去百貨公司買東西，再去朋友家。
text.simplified: A：你明天想要做什么？B：我想先去百货公司买东西，再去朋友家。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ míngtiān xiǎng yào zuò shénme? B: Wǒ xiǎng xiān qù bǎihuò gōngsī mǎi dōngxi, zài qù péngyǒu jiā.
text.english: A: What do you want to do tomorrow? B: I want to go to the department store first to shop, then go to my friend’s place.

items.question: Which time follows 從 — the start or the finish?
items.answer: The start. 從 opens the start; 到 opens the finish: 我從四點到五點半上英文課.

items.wrongSimplified: 我从四点到五点半上英文课。

right.traditional: 我從四點到五點半上英文課。

right.english: I have English class from four to five thirty.
right.simplified: 我从四点到五点半上英文课。

items.question: What is missing in 我從四點五點半上英文課?
items.answer: The finish marker 到: 我從四點到五點半上英文課. 從 and 到 come in a pair.

items.question: Where does 先 go — before the first action or after it?
items.answer: Before it. 先 + first action, 再 + next action: 我先看書，再做功課.

right.english: I read first, then do homework.

items.question: Is the second marker 再 or 在?
items.answer: 再 means “then” in a sequence. 在 is the “at / happening now” word: 我先回家，再去圖書館.

right.pinyin: Wǒ xiān huí jiā, zài qù túshūguǎn.
right.english: I go home first, then go to the library.

items.question: Where does 再 go when the second person is named?
items.answer: After the second subject: 姐姐先唱，妹妹再唱. Do not put 再 before 妹妹.

items.question: Where does 能 go — before the subject or before the verb?
items.answer: Before the verb: 他能來嗎？ 能 does not come before the subject.

items.question: Where does 只 go in 只能?
items.answer: 只 comes before 能: 他只能走. Do not put 只 after the verb.

items.question: The picture shows an injured man. Do I say 他能跑 or 他不能跑?
items.answer: Use 不能: 他受傷了，他不能跑. The injury blocks the action.

right.pinyin: Tā shòushāng le, tā bù néng pǎo.
right.english: He is injured; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 鳥能飛，人不能飛。
text.simplified: 鸟能飞，人不能飞。
text.pinyin: Niǎo néng fēi, rén bù néng fēi.
text.english: Birds can fly; humans cannot fly.

text.traditional: 他現在只能走，不能跑。
text.simplified: 他现在只能走，不能跑。
text.pinyin: Tā xiànzài zhǐ néng zǒu, bù néng pǎo.
text.english: He can only walk right now; he cannot run.

text.traditional: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因為不能睡覺。
text.simplified: 我不能喝太多咖啡，因为不能睡觉。

text.english: I cannot drink too much coffee, because I won’t be able to sleep.

text.traditional: 現在是上課時間，老師說我們不能看手機。

text.traditional: A：在捷運上能吃東西嗎？B：不可以吃東西。
text.simplified: A：在捷运上能吃东西吗？B：不可以吃东西。
text.pinyin: A: Zài jiéyùn shàng néng chī dōngxi ma? B: Bù kěyǐ chī dōngxi.

text.simplified: A：我能在这里用电脑吗？B：可以，没问题。

text.simplified: 今天我有中文课，不能跟你们去玩。

text.traditional: A：那個地方很遠，我們十點鐘能到嗎？B：沒問題，坐捷運很快。
text.simplified: A：那个地方很远，我们十点钟能到吗？B：没问题，坐捷运很快。

text.english: A: That place is very far; can we arrive by ten o’clock? B: No problem; taking the MRT is very fast.

items.question: Why is 我今天比較是忙 not right?
items.answer: 比較 goes before the quality 忙, and 是 is not needed: 我今天比較忙.

items.question: Can I put 很 and 比較 together?
items.answer: No. Choose one degree word: 今天的天氣比較熱. 很 would say “very hot”, not “hotter than the other day”.

items.question: Where does 比較 go when the sentence uses 得?
items.answer: After 跑得: 哥哥跑得比較快. 比較 comes before the quality 快, not before 跑.

text.traditional: 期中考快要到了，老師說我們可以去圖書館對面的大教室看書。
text.simplified: 期中考快要到了，老师说我们可以去图书馆对面的大教室看书。
text.pinyin: Qízhōngkǎo kuàiyào dào le, lǎoshī shuō wǒmen kěyǐ qù túshūguǎn duìmiàn de dà jiàoshì kànshū.
text.english: Midterms are near. The teacher said we may study in the large classroom across from the library.

words.meaning: ending word that shows a new situation

text.traditional: 太好了！在那裡看書很舒服。我們每天都能用那間教室嗎？
text.simplified: 太好了！在那里看书很舒服。我们每天都能用那间教室吗？
text.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Zài nàlǐ kànshū hěn shūfu. Wǒmen měitiān dōu néng yòng nà jiān jiàoshì ma?
text.english: Great! Studying there is comfortable. Can we use that classroom every day?

words.meaning: ending word that shows a new situation
be in the middle of an action; at
very; links a thing to a quality
ending word that makes a yes-no question

text.traditional: 我們班只能禮拜一跟禮拜二下午用。
text.simplified: 我们班只能礼拜一跟礼拜二下午用。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen bān zhǐ néng lǐbài yī gēn lǐbài èr xiàwǔ yòng.
text.english: Our class can only use it Monday and Tuesday afternoons.

text.traditional: 可是這些時間我都有語言交換，不能去。
text.simplified: 可是这些时间我都有语言交换，不能去。
text.pinyin: Kěshì zhèxiē shíjiān wǒ dōu yǒu yǔyán jiāohuàn, bù néng qù.
text.english: But I have language exchange then, so I cannot go.

text.traditional: 別的時間可以嗎？
text.simplified: 别的时间可以吗？
text.pinyin: Biéde shíjiān kěyǐ ma?
text.english: Could you use another time?

words.meaning: ending word that makes a yes-no question

text.traditional: 我朋友最近比較忙，別的時間他沒有空。
text.simplified: 我朋友最近比较忙，别的时间他没有空。
text.pinyin: Wǒ péngyǒu zuìjìn bǐjiào máng, biéde shíjiān tā méi yǒukòng.
text.english: My friend is busier lately and is not free at other times.

words.meaning: relatively; more, with a known comparison

text.traditional: 我們去問老師，也許他可以幫你。
text.simplified: 我们去问老师，也许他可以帮你。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen qù wèn lǎoshī, yěxǔ tā kěyǐ bāng nǐ.
text.english: Let us ask the teacher. Maybe he can help.

text.traditional: 好，希望老師可以幫我。
text.simplified: 好，希望老师可以帮我。
text.pinyin: Hǎo, xīwàng lǎoshī kěyǐ bāng wǒ.
text.english: Okay. I hope the teacher can help me.
